cand.title: Adaptation Canada 2026 Conference
cand.organizationName: Environment and Climate Change Canada and ICLEI Canada
cand.excerpt: Three-day Toronto conference with more than 1,000 participants from across Canada, over 70 sessions, plenaries, study tours and a pre-conference Indigenous Climate Leadership gathering. Government funding and government-official participation make public-sector meeting, catering and delegate lodging demand highly credible, while the organiser and funding arrangement should not be confused with hotel procurement access.
cand.selectionWhy: Prior blocked-promising candidate (no exact date/contact in thin ledger)

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two verified organizer-side relationship contacts: Ewa Jackson, Managing Director, ICLEI Canada, explicitly named as the conference sponsorship contact; and Maria Dasios, Operations Manager, ICLEI Canada, explicitly named in the conference FAQ for volunteer coordination. Ewa is the stronger senior commercial-routing contact; Maria is an operational routing candidate. Neither source establishes hotel procurement authority or contract-signing control. General conference routing: ac2026@iclei.org.
findings.futureEdition: None officially announced was located as of November 15, 2026. No verified Adaptation Canada edition with dates, city or venue falls within December 6, 2026–June 2028. The verified 2026 conference is past. ICLEI’s post-event page promotes Livable Cities Forum 2027, a different event, not the next Adaptation Canada edition.
findings.hotelProductFit: Strong historical accommodation fit is directly evidenced: the target Radisson already had a published 2026 room block. Inference using the supplied 157-room capacity and approximately 240-theatre largest room: this 1,000-plus-participant conference is too large for exclusive housing or full plenary delivery at the Radisson. Appropriate roles are a limited delegate/speaker/VIP block and suitably sized side meetings, subject to actual requirements. This is a downtown waterfront city-hotel opportunity, not a resort buyout. Do not assume 15–109 peak rooms were actually required; no block quantity is published. Do not promise food-and-beverage functions without separately confirming restaurant/lounge and catering operations.
findings.venueCommitments: Historical 2026 venue: The Westin Harbour Castle, 1 Harbour Square, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. It is in Toronto proper, downtown on the waterfront, within the target territory—not an out-of-town resort or an MTCC/Exhibition Place venue. The edition-specific venue and FAQ establish the venue selection, not the terms of its contract. No future venue commitment was located.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified editions: April 12–14, 2016, Shaw Centre, Ottawa, Ontario; February 19–21, 2020, Sheraton Vancouver Wall Centre, Vancouver, British Columbia; September 22–24, 2026, The Westin Harbour Castle, Toronto, Ontario. ICLEI calls 2026 the third edition. This establishes recurrence and destination rotation, not an annual/biennial schedule or a Toronto return.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Two hotels are explicitly listed in the edition-specific FAQ: The Westin Harbour Castle and Radisson Blu, identifiable as Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown by its published telephone number. Westin: “Special room rates at the Westin Harbour Castle have been negotiated for attendees of Adaptation Canada 2026”; $429/night plus taxes, an official Passkey booking link, or telephone booking using group code ICL / ICLEI Canada Adaptation Canada Conference Sep2026. Radisson: “Yes, we also have a block of rooms on reserve at the Radisson Blu.” Individual reservations were directed to 437-886-9667 or frontdesk@radissonblutoronto.com, using group name “Adaptation Canada 2026,” guaranteed by credit card. These are historical edition-specific blocks, including one at the target hotel—not merely a preferred-hotel list. No independent housing bureau or open hotel RFP was identified; Passkey alone does not establish a housing bureau. Block sizes, Radisson rate, pickup, room nights and commercial terms are unpublished in the reviewed material.
findings.organizationStructure: ICLEI Canada delivered/organized the 2026 conference, supported by partners and funded in part by the Government of Canada. ICLEI’s team page describes its governance as that of a non-profit organization. ECCC is a funder and advisory participant; it should not be treated as the hotel buyer solely because of funding or government attendance. No external PCO, DMC, housing agency or hotel contracting intermediary was identified. Legal event ownership and hotel signatory remain unverified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Westin held the main venue and a negotiated lodging block, offering the practical advantage of accommodation at the conference venue. Radisson was itself a second published block, presented under the FAQ’s budget-friendly alternatives question. This supports a secondary accommodation role but does not prove Westin sold out, a capacity shortage occurred, or any room nights materialized. No other edition-specific lodging hotel was identified.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: First reconcile the hotel’s own Adaptation Canada 2026 group file, contracted allotment, actual pickup, room nights, rate and organizer contact. Then request a brief post-event review with Ewa Jackson, copying ac2026@iclei.org; use Maria Dasios to route operational questions if needed. Ask who contracted the Radisson block, whether another edition is planned, how destination selection works, and when accommodation sourcing would start. Only after a Toronto requirement is confirmed, propose a right-sized return delegate/speaker block; validate catering before offering receptions. Do not launch an RFP response or assign forecast rooms/revenue now.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Closed by event date: the conference ran September 22–24, 2026; the Indigenous Climate Leadership gathering was September 21. The September 28 government release is publication provenance, not an activity date. Historical booking instructions still online are not evidence of current open inventory or an actionable upcoming opportunity. Pursue a post-event account review, not a 2026 availability pitch.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional relationship opportunity, not confirmed future demand. Because Radisson was already publicly included in the 2026 accommodation programme, retaining or expanding that organizer relationship is more appropriate than assuming a first-time competitive displacement. A future Adaptation Canada edition would only generate relevant Radisson demand if Toronto is selected again and a lodging requirement exists. Rotation across Ottawa, Vancouver and Toronto gives no basis for assuming that return or a fixed procurement cycle.
